route53-dnsfw-filters-inbound-endpoint-q: When a DNS Firewall rule group is associated with a VPC's Route 53 VPC Resolver, DNS Firewall filters the DNS queries that pass through Resolver endpoints from on-premises resources into that same VPC.
route53-faq-elb-failover-no-route53-heal: When failover for ELB endpoints relies on Evaluate Target Health instead of your own health checks, Amazon Route 53 generates no specific CloudWatch metrics for those endpoints; Elastic Load Balancing publishes metrics that show the health of the load balancer and the number of healthy instances behind it.
route53-faq-traffic-policy-vs-policy-rec: A traffic policy is the set of rules that you define to route end users' requests to one of your application's endpoints; by itself it does not affect how end users are routed, because it is not yet associated with your application's DNS name.
route53-hc-calculated-disabled-child-hea: If you disable a health check that a calculated health check monitors, Amazon Route 53 considers the disabled health check to be healthy when it calculates whether the calculated health check is healthy.
route53-reusable-delegation-set-api-only: Reusable delegation sets are not available in the Amazon Route 53 console. A reusable delegation set lets you tell your registrar to use the same four name servers for all the domains that you want Route 53 to serve, which makes it simpler to migrate DNS service to Route 53.
